question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A speech by an actor at the end of a play
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Epilogue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Epilogue" means a speech or piece of writing delivered by an actor at the end of a play, or a short concluding section at the end of a literary work, often summing up or commenting on what has happened. (नाटक के अंत में दिया गया भाषण)
◦ Example: The actor delivered a moving epilogue, thanking the audience for their support.

• The word comes from the Greek "epilogos", meaning "conclusion" — "epi-" (upon/in addition) + "logos" (word/speech).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Prologue (प्रस्तावना): An introduction or preface, especially a speech given at the beginning of a play, that sets the scene for what follows.

• Option 2: Monologue (एकालाप): A long speech given by one actor/character alone, often expressing his/her private thoughts, regardless of its position in the play.

• Option 4: Duologue (द्विसंवाद): A conversation or dramatic piece involving only two speakers/actors.

NOTE

• Remember the contrast: Prologue = beginning, Epilogue = end.

• Other related one-word substitutes often asked in SSC: Soliloquy (a character speaking his thoughts aloud to himself), Elegy (a poem of mourning for the dead), Eulogy (a speech praising someone, often at their funeral).

question:
Select the option that is OPPOSITE in meaning to the given word.
Incompetent
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Dexterous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Incompetent" means lacking the necessary skill or ability to do something successfully. (अयोग्य/अक्षम)

• Its opposite is "Dexterous", which means skilful in using one's hands or mind; adroit and capable. (कुशल/निपुण)
◦ Example: The dexterous surgeon completed the operation in record time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Forlorn (निराश्रित/उदास): Pitifully sad and lonely; abandoned. It is not an antonym of "incompetent".

• Option 2: Desperate (हताश): Having lost all hope; reckless due to despair. Not related to skill/competence.

• Option 3: Hopeless (निराश): Feeling or causing despair; also informally used to mean "incompetent" (a near-synonym, not an antonym).

NOTE

• Do not confuse "Hopeless" (which can be a synonym of incompetent in informal usage) with the required antonym.

• Other synonyms of "Dexterous": adept, proficient, skilful, competent, deft.

• Other synonyms of "Incompetent": inept, unskilled, inefficient, unqualified.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Someone who lives in solitude
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Recluse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Recluse" means a person who lives a solitary life and deliberately avoids the company of others. (एकांतवासी)
◦ Example: After his wife's death, he became a recluse and rarely left his house.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Metropolitan (महानगरीय): Relating to a large, busy city; a resident of a large city — the opposite idea of solitude.

• Option 2: Cosmopolitan (विश्वजनीन): Familiar with and at ease in many different countries and cultures; someone comfortable with people from all over the world — again the opposite of a solitary person.

• Option 4: Refugee (शरणार्थी): A person forced to leave their country to escape war, persecution, or natural disaster.

NOTE

• Other similar one-word substitutes: Hermit (a person living in solitude, often for religious reasons), Misanthrope (a person who dislikes mankind), Introvert (a shy, reticent person).

• Do not confuse "Recluse" with "Refugee" — both can suggest being "away" from normal society, but only Recluse specifically means choosing solitude.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. Lord Ganesha, the Destroyer of Obstacles, is worshipped for his wisdom and brilliance.
B. People adore the goddess Lakshmi and Lord Ganesha on Diwali.
C. This 'New Year' i.e., Diwali is marked by merchants establishing new account books.
D. Goddess Lakshmi is also worshipped on Diwali for wealth and success.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. BADC.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A coherent paragraph must open with a general statement that introduces the topic, followed by sentences that logically elaborate on it, and finally move to a related but distinct idea.

• Sentence B is the best opening sentence — it introduces both deities, Lakshmi and Ganesha, who are worshipped on Diwali, and sets up the topic for the rest of the paragraph.

• Sentence A logically follows B, elaborating specifically on Lord Ganesha and why he is worshipped (wisdom and brilliance).

• Sentence D follows next — the word "also" in "Goddess Lakshmi is also worshipped..." signals that it is adding to the previous idea about worship (paralleling sentence A, now for Lakshmi).

• Sentence C logically comes last, introducing a new but related idea — that Diwali marks the "New Year" for merchants, who start new account books.
◦ Reading the paragraph in order: B → A → D → C forms a smooth, logical flow from "who is worshipped on Diwali" to "why each deity is worshipped" to "what else Diwali signifies".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2, i.e., BADC.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (DABC) is incorrect because it starts with D ("also worshipped"), which needs a prior sentence to make sense of the word "also" — there is no antecedent for it at the start.

• Option 3 (ADBC) is incorrect because starting with A jumps directly into detail about Ganesha without first introducing the general topic of Diwali worship.

• Option 4 (CDBA) is incorrect because starting with C ("This 'New Year'...") uses the word "This", which requires Diwali to have already been introduced as a festival earlier in the paragraph — but no such introduction precedes it in this order.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, always check for words like "this", "also", "however", "therefore" — these are cohesion clues that indicate a sentence cannot be the opening line, since they refer back to something already mentioned.

• Identify the most general, standalone sentence as your starting point, then trace pronouns/connectors to build the chain.

question:
Identify the option that can be substituted as the correct idiom for the underlined part of the given sentence.
As soon as the principal came to know about the inspection in the school, he put everything in perfect order.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Apple pie order.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Apple pie order" means in perfect order; extremely neat and well-organised. (पूर्णतः व्यवस्थित/करीने से रखा हुआ)
◦ Example: Before the guests arrived, she had put the whole house in apple pie order.

• In the given sentence, the principal arranged everything neatly ahead of the inspection, which matches exactly the meaning of "apple pie order".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Apple of discord (कलह का कारण): Something that causes trouble, disagreement, or a quarrel.
◦ Example: The disputed land became an apple of discord between the two brothers.

• Option 3: Alley apple (बेकार वस्तु): A worthless or discarded object; informally can also mean a lump of horse dung found in the street.

• Option 4: Apple of one's eye (आँखों का तारा): A person or thing that someone cherishes above all others.
◦ Example: His youngest daughter is the apple of his eye.

NOTE

• Other "apple" idioms commonly asked in SSC: "A bad apple" (a person who has a bad influence on others), "Upset the apple cart" (to spoil a plan), "Apples and oranges" (things too different to compare).

question:
Select the correct idiom that can substitute the italicised group of words in the given sentence.
Shelley has been contemplating for a few days but still has not decided to quit the job.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. chewing the cud.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Chewing the cud" means to think deeply about something; to ponder or reflect over an issue for a long time before deciding. (गहराई से सोचना/मनन करना)
◦ Example: He has been chewing the cud over the job offer for a week now.

• In the given sentence, Shelley has been thinking over/pondering the decision to quit her job for several days, which matches "chewing the cud".

• The idiom originates from the way cows and other ruminant animals repeatedly chew their food (cud) to digest it slowly — used figuratively for slow, deliberate thinking.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Biting the dust (हार जाना/मर जाना): To fail, be defeated, or die.
◦ Example: Many small businesses bit the dust during the recession.

• Option 3: Cooling one's heels (इंतजार करना): To be kept waiting for a long time.
◦ Example: The visitors were left cooling their heels outside the manager's office.

• Option 4: Getting into hot waters (मुसीबत में पड़ना): To get into trouble or a difficult situation.

NOTE

• Other idioms of thinking/deliberating: "To rack one's brains" (to think very hard), "To weigh the pros and cons" (to carefully consider advantages and disadvantages), "To sleep on it" (to delay a decision until the next day to think it over).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Raghav had a good ______ for stage plays.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. troupe.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Troupe" means a group or company of actors, singers, dancers, or other performers, especially one that travels to perform.

• In the given sentence, "Raghav had a good troupe for stage plays" means Raghav had a good company/group of performers for staging plays, which fits the context of "stage plays" perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Trip" means a journey from one place to another; it does not fit the context of stage plays.

• Option 2: "Trope" means a figurative or metaphorical use of a word/expression, or a recurring theme/device in literature; it does not fit here.

• Option 3: "Troop" means a group of soldiers, or more generally a group of people/animals moving together; it is not specifically related to performing arts and does not fit the sense of "for stage plays" as well as "troupe" does.

NOTE

• "Troupe", "troop", "trope" and "trip" are commonly confused homophones/near-homophones in SSC exams because of their similar spelling and pronunciation.

• Remember: Troupe = group of performers, Troop = group of soldiers, Trope = a figure of speech/recurring motif, Trip = a journey.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.
We hardly knew nothing / about the manager / who had recently joined.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. We hardly knew nothing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hardly" is a negative adverb (like "scarcely", "barely", "seldom"). English does not allow two negative words in the same clause (a "double negative") — using "hardly" together with "nothing" creates an incorrect double negative.

• Rule: "Hardly/scarcely/barely" must be followed by "anything/anyone/any", not by another negative word like "nothing/no one/none".

• The correct sentence should read: "We hardly knew anything about the manager who had recently joined."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 ("No error") is incorrect because the sentence does contain a grammatical error (the double negative).

• Option 3 ("about the manager") is grammatically correct as written; it is not the erroneous part.

• Option 4 ("who had recently joined") is grammatically correct as written; it is not the erroneous part.

NOTE

• Similar double-negative errors to watch for: "I don't have no money" (should be "I don't have any money"), "He can't hardly walk" (should be "He can hardly walk").

• Words like hardly, scarcely, barely, seldom, rarely, never already carry negative meaning and should never be paired with another negative word in the same clause.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
Here / come / the bus / for Lucknow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. come.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement: A singular subject must take a singular verb, and a plural subject must take a plural verb.

• Here, the subject is "the bus", which is singular, so it must take the singular verb "comes", not the plural/base form "come".

• The correct sentence should read: "Here comes the bus for Lucknow."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 ("for Lucknow") is grammatically correct as written; it correctly names the bus's destination.

• Option 2 ("the bus") is grammatically correct as written; it is the correct singular subject.

• Option 4 ("Here") is grammatically correct as written; it correctly signals the inverted sentence structure ("Here comes...").

NOTE

• With sentences beginning with "Here" or "There" followed by inversion (Here comes/There goes), the verb must still agree with the subject that follows it, not with "Here/There".

• Similar examples: "Here comes the train." (singular) vs. "Here come the guests." (plural).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Sandwitch.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Sandwitch" is incorrectly spelt. The correct spelling is "Sandwich" — two or more slices of bread with a filling of meat, cheese, vegetables, etc., placed between them.

• Spelling key: SAND + WICH, not "sand + witch". The word is named after John Montagu, the 4th Earl of Sandwich, who is said to have popularised eating food this way.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Tour" is correctly spelt — a journey or trip, especially one involving a series of stops.

• Option 2: "Triumph" is correctly spelt — a great victory or achievement.

• Option 4: "Process" is correctly spelt — a series of actions or steps taken to achieve a particular end.

NOTE

• Commonly misspelt words similar in pattern to "sandwich": rhythm, restaurant, definitely, embarrass, occurrence, questionnaire.

• Always be careful with words that sound like they contain another word (e.g., "sandwich" sounding like it might contain "witch") — spell by rule, not by sound.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
The growing population of India will have been controlled by the Indian government by 2040.
option_1: By 2040, the Indian population will have continued to grow uncontrollably
option_2: By 2040, the Indian government will have controlled the growing population of India.
option_3: By 2040, the Indian government is successfully controlling the growing population of India.
option_4: The Indian population will have stabilised by 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. By 2040, the Indian government will have controlled the growing population of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence, "The growing population of India will have been controlled by the Indian government by 2040", is in the passive voice, Future Perfect Tense.

• Rule — Future Perfect Tense:
◦ Passive: Object + will have been + V3 + by + Subject
◦ Active: Subject + will have + V3 + Object

• Applying the rule: the agent "the Indian government" becomes the subject; the auxiliary changes from "will have been" to "will have"; the past participle "controlled" is retained as the main verb; and the object "the growing population of India" becomes the object of the active sentence, with the time phrase "by 2040" retained.
◦ Active: By 2040, the Indian government will have controlled the growing population of India.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because it changes the meaning entirely — it suggests the population will keep growing uncontrollably, the opposite of the original sentence's meaning (that it will be controlled).

• Option 3 is incorrect because "is successfully controlling" is in the Present Continuous Tense, not the Future Perfect Tense required to match the original sentence.

• Option 4 is incorrect because it changes both the subject (to "the Indian population" instead of "the Indian government") and the year (2022 instead of 2040), and uses a different verb ("stabilised"), altering the original meaning.

NOTE

• In active-passive conversion questions, always first identify the tense of the given sentence, then apply the fixed active/passive formula for that specific tense — do not rely only on "sounds correct".

• Future Perfect active/passive formulas are frequently tested in SSC exams alongside Simple Future and Future Continuous.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
One who loves mankind
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Philanthropist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Philanthropist" means a person who seeks to promote the welfare of others, especially by donating money generously; one who loves and works for the good of mankind. (परोपकारी/मानवता-प्रेमी)
◦ Example: The philanthropist donated millions of rupees to build schools for underprivileged children.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Atheist (नास्तिक): A person who does not believe in the existence of God.

• Option 2: Pessimist (निराशावादी): A person who tends to see the worst aspect of things or expects the worst outcome.

• Option 3: Optimist (आशावादी): A person who is hopeful and confident about the future.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "Philanthropist" (one who loves mankind and helps others) with "Misanthrope" (one who hates/dislikes mankind) — they are opposites.

• Other related one-word substitutes: Humanitarian (a person concerned with human welfare), Altruist (a person who is unselfishly concerned for the well-being of others).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Allimony.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Allimony" is incorrectly spelt. The correct spelling is "Alimony" — a sum of money paid regularly by one spouse to another following a separation or divorce.

• Spelling key: A + LIMONY — only a single "l", not double "ll".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Structural" is correctly spelt — relating to the structure or framework of something.

• Option 3: "Hallucinate" is correctly spelt — to experience a seemingly real perception of something not actually present (usually due to illness or a drug).

• Option 4: "Halloween" is correctly spelt — the festival observed on 31 October.

NOTE

• Watch for words that are commonly mis-doubled or under-doubled in consonants: "Alimony" (single l), but "Hallucinate" and "Halloween" (double l) — spelling of double consonants must be memorised word by word, not by a general rule.

• Other frequently confused legal/formal terms: alimony, testimony, matrimony, ceremony — all end in "-mony" with a single "m".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Judicious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Sensible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Judicious" means having, showing, or done with good judgement or sense; sensible and wise, especially in practical matters. (विवेकपूर्ण/समझदार)
◦ Example: She made a judicious decision to invest her savings carefully.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Imprudent (अविवेकपूर्ण): Not showing care for the consequences of an action; unwise — this is an antonym, not a synonym, of "judicious".

• Option 3: Careless (लापरवाह): Not giving sufficient attention or thought to avoiding harm or errors — again opposite in meaning.

• Option 4: Short-sighted (अदूरदर्शी): Lacking imagination or foresight about future consequences — also opposite in meaning.

NOTE

• Be careful: three of the four options here (Imprudent, Careless, Short-sighted) are all antonyms of "Judicious", and only one (Sensible) is the true synonym — read the question stem carefully to check whether it asks for synonym or antonym.

• Other synonyms of "Judicious": prudent, wise, discerning, shrewd, sound.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Which _________ do you usually take to reach your office?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. route.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Route" means a way or course taken in getting from a starting point to a destination. In the given sentence, it correctly fits the context of the path taken to reach the office.

• The other options are homophones/near-homophones of "route" but carry entirely different meanings, making them unsuitable in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Root" means the part of a plant that grows underground, or the source/origin of something — it does not fit the context of travelling.

• Option 3: "Rout" means a decisive/overwhelming defeat, or to defeat someone decisively — it does not fit the context.

• Option 4: "Rude" means offensive or impolite in manner or speech — it does not fit the context at all.

NOTE

• "Route" and "Root" are commonly confused homophones in SSC exams: Route = path/way, Root = part of a plant/origin.

• Other similar commonly confused word pairs: Rout vs. Route vs. Root, Rain vs. Reign vs. Rein, Right vs. Rite vs. Write.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Extol
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Praise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Extol" means to praise enthusiastically; to speak highly of someone or something. (प्रशंसा करना/गुणगान करना)
◦ Example: The critics extolled the young singer's extraordinary talent.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Reward (पुरस्कार): Something given in recognition of a service, effort or achievement — not the same as verbally praising.

• Option 2: Punish (दंड देना): To inflict a penalty for wrongdoing — an antonym, not a synonym.

• Option 3: Dismay (निराशा): A feeling of concern or distress caused by something unexpected — opposite in tone to "extol".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Extol": eulogise, laud, glorify, exalt, commend.

• Antonyms of "Extol": criticise, condemn, denounce, disparage.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Author's explanatory remarks at the beginning of a book
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Preface.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Preface" means an introduction to a book, typically stating its subject, scope, or reason for being written, usually written by the author. (प्रस्तावना/भूमिका)
◦ Example: In the preface, the author explained why she decided to write about her grandmother's life.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Foreward" (a variant spelling of "Foreword") refers to a short introductory statement, typically written by a person other than the author, at the beginning of a book — since the question specifies the author's own remarks, "Preface" is the more precise fit.

• Option 3: Bibliography (ग्रंथ-सूची): A list of books/sources referred to or used by the author, usually placed at the end of a book.

• Option 4: Biography (जीवनी): A written account of a person's life, written by someone else.

NOTE

• Distinguish: Preface = written by the author, about the book itself; Foreword = written by someone else (often a notable person), to introduce/endorse the book.

• Other related terms: Prologue (an introduction to a literary/dramatic work, part of the narrative itself), Introduction (opening section that presents the topic), Epilogue (a concluding section at the end).

question: Identify how will you say that "The doctor treated the victims of the violence very carefully", in the passive voice.
option_1: The doctor was very careful while providing treatment to the victims
option_2: The doctor's care was shown to the victims of the violence
option_3: The victims of the violence were treated very carefully by the doctor
option_4: The victims were treated attentively by the doctor
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The victims of the violence were treated very carefully by the doctor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "The doctor treated the victims of the violence very carefully" is in the Active Voice, Simple Past Tense.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + V2 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "the victims of the violence" becomes the subject; since it is plural, the auxiliary used is "were"; the verb "treated" (already V2/V3 form) is retained as the past participle; "the doctor" becomes the agent introduced by "by"; and the adverb "very carefully" is retained in its original position/meaning.
◦ Passive: The victims of the violence were treated very carefully by the doctor.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because it changes the meaning of the sentence — it describes the doctor's own carefulness rather than stating that the victims were treated carefully, and it is not a passive transformation of the original sentence.

• Option 2 is incorrect because it changes the verb from "treated" to "care was shown", altering the original meaning and not being a direct/faithful passive transformation.

• Option 4 is incorrect because it drops the crucial detail "of the violence" (referring to who the victims are victims of) and changes "very carefully" to "attentively", altering the original wording and meaning.

NOTE

• When converting active to passive, always preserve the tense, the adverbs, and all descriptive phrases exactly as given — do not substitute synonyms or drop details, as this changes the sentence's original meaning.

• Simple Past Tense active/passive formulas are among the most frequently tested in SSC voice-change questions.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below. While the first and the last sentences (S1 and S6) are in the correct order, the sentences in between are jumbled up. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
S1. He sat in his seat
A. hardly showing any signs of hearing
B. beside the bed,
C. gazing sternly
D. at the patient's face
S6. what they were saying to him.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. BCDA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The paragraph must read as one continuous, grammatically connected sentence from S1 to S6.

• After S1 "He sat in his seat", the most natural continuation is B ("beside the bed,"), describing the location of his seat.

• This is followed by C ("gazing sternly"), describing his action/expression while seated.

• Next comes D ("at the patient's face"), completing the phrase "gazing sternly at" by specifying what he was gazing at.

• Finally, A ("hardly showing any signs of hearing") connects smoothly to S6 ("what they were saying to him"), since "hearing" logically takes "what they were saying to him" as its object.
◦ Full sentence: "He sat in his seat beside the bed, gazing sternly at the patient's face, hardly showing any signs of hearing what they were saying to him."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2, i.e., BCDA.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (DABC) is incorrect because it places D ("at the patient's face") immediately after S1, which is grammatically disconnected — "at the patient's face" has no preceding verb like "gazing" to attach to at that point.

• Option 3 (DCAB) is incorrect for the same reason — D cannot immediately follow S1, and the resulting sequence does not form a grammatically coherent phrase.

• Option 4 (DBAC) is incorrect because it similarly begins with D right after S1 and disrupts the logical phrase "gazing sternly at the patient's face".

NOTE

• In parajumbles with fixed first/last sentences, look for participle phrases (e.g., "gazing sternly", "hardly showing") and their objects — these must stay adjacent to the phrase they complete/modify.

• Always read the fully reconstructed sentence to check that it is grammatically complete and makes logical sense from start to end.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Hundreds of firms went bankrupt during the _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. recession.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Recession" means a period of temporary economic decline during which trade and industrial activity are reduced, generally identified by a fall in GDP for two successive quarters. It fits the context of firms going bankrupt.
◦ Example: Many small businesses shut down during the recession of 2008.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Recission" is not a standard English word (the correct term for cancellation of a contract is "rescission"), and it does not fit this economic context.

• Option 2: "Revision" means the action of reviewing and altering something, typically a text or plan — it does not fit the context of firms going bankrupt.

• Option 3: "Remission" means a temporary diminution of the severity of a disease or pain, or the cancellation of a debt/penalty — it does not fit the context here.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "Recession" (economic downturn) with "Rescission" (cancellation/revocation of a contract or agreement) — they are spelled and pronounced similarly but mean entirely different things.

• Related economic terms often tested: Depression (a severe, prolonged recession), Inflation (a general rise in prices), Stagnation (a period of little or no economic growth).

Changes to the earth's climate, driven by increased (1)_______ of heat-trapping greenhouse gases, are already having widespread effects on the environment. Shrinking of glaciers and ice sheets, occurrence of shifts in flower/plant blooming times, etc., are creating an overall (2)_________ in the natural ecosystem. Conditions like the rise in sea-levels and saltwater intrusion have advanced to the point where whole (3)____________ have had to relocate, while protracted droughts are putting people at risk of (4)_________. The effects of human-caused global warming are (5)_______ for people alive today and will worsen as long as humans keep feeding greenhouse gases into the atmosphere.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. emission.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage discusses climate change being driven by increased release of heat-trapping greenhouse gases. The word "emission" means the production and discharge of something, especially gas or radiation, into the atmosphere — this exactly fits the context of greenhouse gases being released.

• Contextual clue: The phrase "heat-trapping greenhouse gases" that follows the blank confirms that the passage is talking about the release/discharge of gases, which is precisely what "emission" refers to.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "feeding" does not fit — while the passage later uses "feeding greenhouse gases into the atmosphere" as a verb phrase, the blank here requires a noun describing the driving cause of climate change (the release of gases), not the act of "feeding".

• Option 3: "creation" does not fit contextually — the passage is about the release/discharge of already-produced gases into the atmosphere, not their "creation".

• Option 4: "fertilisation" is unrelated to greenhouse gases and climate change; it refers to the process of fertilising, which is irrelevant here.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always read the words immediately before and after the blank — here, "increased ___ of heat-trapping greenhouse gases" clearly calls for a noun meaning "release/discharge", which only "emission" provides.

• Related word: "emit" (verb) — to emit greenhouse gases; "emission" (noun) — the release of greenhouse gases.

• Contextual clue: The phrase "in the natural ecosystem" following the blank supports a word describing disruption/disturbance to the ecosystem's normal balance, which "imbalance" provides.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

NOTE

• Related words: disequilibrium, disruption, disturbance — all synonyms suited to describing an ecosystem thrown off balance.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. communities.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage states that due to rising sea-levels and saltwater intrusion, groups of people living together in a particular area have had to relocate. The word "communities" refers to groups of people living in the same place or sharing particular characteristics — exactly what would need to relocate due to sea-level rise.

• Contextual clue: The verb "have had to relocate" requires a plural noun referring to groups of people/settlements, which "communities" provides in a natural, idiomatic way (as in "coastal communities").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "mobs" means disorderly crowds of people, often with negative/unruly connotations — it does not fit the neutral, factual tone of the passage about people relocating due to climate change.

• Option 2: "people" is grammatically possible but less precise and less idiomatic than "communities" in this context — SSC cloze passages favour the more specific, contextually apt term, since "whole communities" (as in whole towns/settlements) is the standard collocation used in climate-change writing, unlike "whole people".

• Option 4: "conditions" does not fit — "conditions" cannot logically "relocate"; only people/settlements can relocate.

NOTE

• Watch for common collocations in formal/academic English writing about climate change: "whole communities relocating", "coastal communities at risk" — these are frequently tested phrases.

• "Whole" as a modifier before a noun (as in "whole communities") is a strong contextual signal favouring a noun denoting a group/settlement rather than a generic word like "people".

solution_text:

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage states that "protracted droughts" (long-lasting periods of low rainfall) are putting people at risk. The word "famine" means an extreme scarcity of food, often as a direct result of prolonged drought — this is the standard, logical consequence of droughts.

• Contextual clue: The word "protracted droughts" immediately before the blank is the key clue — prolonged droughts lead to crop failure and food scarcity, i.e., famine.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "pregnancy" has no logical connection with droughts; it is medically and contextually irrelevant here.

• Option 3: "overpopulation" refers to too many people in an area relative to resources — it is not a direct or typical consequence of drought, and does not fit the cause-effect relationship the sentence sets up.

• Option 4: "surgery" is a medical procedure entirely unrelated to the effects of drought.

NOTE

• Standard cause-effect pairing frequently tested in SSC comprehension/cloze passages: drought → famine, flood → displacement, heatwave → drought.

• Related vocabulary: "scarcity", "starvation", and "food insecurity" are near-synonyms often used alongside "famine" in climate-change contexts.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. irreversible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage concludes that the effects of human-caused global warming are severe for people today "and will worsen as long as humans keep feeding greenhouse gases into the atmosphere". The word "irreversible" means not able to be changed back to a previous state/condition — conveying that the damage already done cannot be undone, which matches this concluding, cautionary tone.

• Contextual clue: The following clause, "will worsen as long as...", indicates that the effects are already fixed/lasting and only going to get worse, not something that can be reversed — supporting "irreversible" as the fitting word.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "heart breaking" describes an emotional reaction (deep sadness), which does not fit the objective, factual/scientific tone of the passage about lasting physical effects.

• Option 2: "contradictory" means mutually opposed or inconsistent — this makes no logical sense in describing the effects of global warming, which are consistent, not self-contradicting.

• Option 4: "conditional" means dependent on something else being true; this does not fit, since the sentence describes effects that are already happening and will continue to worsen, not effects contingent on a condition.

NOTE

• The passage's closing sentence about effects worsening "as long as humans keep feeding greenhouse gases into the atmosphere" is a strong contextual clue pointing to permanence/non-reversibility, making "irreversible" the logical choice.

• Related vocabulary: "irrevocable", "permanent", "lasting" — near-synonyms of "irreversible" often tested in similar contexts; contrast with "reversible" or "temporary".
